title: Updated Protocols for Serving Quarantine Orders at Home and Support Measures for Persons with Disabilities, the Young and the Elderly
what_it_is: Updated Protocols for Serving Quarantine Orders at Home and Support Measures for Persons with Disabilities, the Young and the Elderly

sections.label: QO and SHN personnel queries
sections.summary: Questions ask about QO and SHN personnel numbers, service provider capacity, experience improvements, feedback, time limits, August 2021 feedback, and backup manpower plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the current number of personnel involved in administering QO and SHN process; (b) whether the service providers are able to cope with the increased numbers of people on QO and SHN; (c) whether the overall experience can be improved; and (d) how many cases of adverse feedback have been received to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the stipulated time limit to address public queries on their QOs; (b) in August 2021, what is the number of feedback that the Ministry has received concerning belated issuances of QOs or problematic communications and how are they addressed; and (c) whether the Ministry has a backup plan to deploy additional manpower in case of a surge in COVID-19 infections.

sections.label: COVID-19 patient conveyance and capacity
sections.summary: Questions ask about pickup times for patients aged 70 and above, home recovery hospitalisations, general ward and ambulance capacity, ICU and isolation bed utilisation, ICU expansion plans, criteria, and infection spikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) for the last 14 days, what is (i) the average time taken to pick up COVID-19 patients aged 70 and above for conveyance to a hospital, from the time they are confirmed positive by the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test and (ii) the number of COVID-19 patients in home recovery and community care facilities who turned ill and required hospitalisation; and (b) in the longer run what is the capacity of general wards in public hospitals and SCDF ambulances that the Ministry expects to set aside for COVID-19 patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health regarding COVID-19 patients (a) for the past three months, what are the weekly capacity and utilisation rates of (i) ICU beds (ii) isolation beds in hospitals and (iii) community care facilities; (b) what are the plans and associated lead time to increase ICU capacity if required; (c) what are the criteria used to determine the need to increase ICU capacity; (d) whether the recent spike in COVID-19 infections has led to a congruent spike in ICU and oxygen supplementation patients; (e) if so, why; and (f) if not, why.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Government will (i) consider providing more Antigen Rapid Test (ART) kits to each Singaporean household beyond the three provided by Temasek Foundation and (ii) work with distributors of ART kits to lower the retail price,  given the sharp rise in COVID-19 cases in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Currently, about 15% of hospital beds in the acute public hospitals are used for around 10% of all COVID-19 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In the last three months, ICU bed occupancy has increased from 26% to 53%.

sections.label: ICU bed capacity increase
sections.summary: ICU bed capacity has been increased by 74 beds, for a total of 187 beds dedicated to COVID-19 patients with severe conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We are closely monitoring ICU trends, in particular.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We have increased the ICU bed capacity by 74 beds, for a total of 187 beds dedicated to COVID-19 patients with severe conditions.

sections.label: Mild infections and home recovery
sections.summary: Over 98% of infected individuals have mild or no symptoms and 0.3% needed ICU care or died, so home recovery is the default protocol except for severe, elderly, or co-morbid cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The vast majority – over 98% – of infected individuals have mild or no symptoms and only 0.3% have needed ICU care or have, sadly, passed on.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This is a result of having vaccinated most of our population, who will only experience mild illness if they suffer a breakthrough infection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Thus, we are making home recovery the default protocol for infected individuals, unless they have severe symptoms, are elderly, or have underlying co-morbidities that make them more susceptible to severe disease outcomes.

sections.label: Home quarantine and SHN adjustments
sections.summary: Hospital resources are prioritised for the severely ill, and QO and SHN regimes are adjusted to allow suitable individuals and fully vaccinated travellers to recover or quarantine at home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This ensures that our hospital and medical treatment resources are prioritised for those who are, or could be, severely ill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We have also adjusted our QO regime to allow individuals who are less likely to fall severely ill with COVID-19 and whose homes are suitable for home recovery, to quarantine at home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: After the original quarantined individual is confirmed to have COVID-19 and has been served an Isolation Order, the other household members should self-register for quarantine as well, in order for the whole family to recover and be quarantined together at home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We will also increasingly allow fully vaccinated travellers who need to serve an SHN to do so at home.

sections.label: P2P drivers on QO
sections.summary: Between January and September this year, around 3,300 point-to-point drivers and riders were placed on QOs and can apply for a QO Allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Between January and September this year, around 3,300 point-to-point (P2P) drivers and riders have been placed on QOs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These individuals, along with others whose livelihoods have been affected by QOs, can apply for a QO Allowance to help cushion the financial impact.

sections.label: SASH clinic COVID-19 cases
sections.summary: Of total COVID-19 cases found in the last eight weeks at SASH clinics, 7% had initially tested positive on self-test ART kits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Of the total COVID-19 cases identified in the last eight weeks via the PCR test at Swab and Send Home (SASH) clinics, 7% had, initially, tested positive using the self-test ART kits before coming forward for their confirmatory PCR test.

sections.label: Fixed day of discharge
sections.summary: A fixed discharge day exists because vaccinated persons' viral load drops quickly, so NCID can safely discharge them on day 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The reason why there is now a fixed day of discharge is because, once a person is vaccinated, the viral load drops very quickly, especially after day 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And by day 10, NCID finds that they cannot culture the virus anymore because the viral load becomes quite low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Which is why we can safely discharge patients who are vaccinated on day 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The IT system needs to keep up with that policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, in the next few days, the TraceTogether issue will be resolved as we will also synchronise the removal of the alert in line with the discharge day.

sections.label: Caller attendance rate
sections.summary: As of yesterday, almost 70% of callers could be attended to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of yesterday, when I checked, we are able to attend to almost 70% of the callers.

sections.label: Streamlining travel measures
sections.summary: The changing situation means more travellers may do SHN, with further streamlining, optimising and alignment of measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Partly, this is a result of the changing situation and, actually, today, an increasing number of travellers are allowed to do an SHN and you will see that we will have further and further streamlining, optimising and alignment of our various measures.

sections.label: Household members registration call
sections.summary: The call is for all household members of a contact to register, not only some of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The call is for all of us to be responsible and for the household members of a contact, indeed, to register.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are not asking for only some of them to register.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are asking for all of them to register.

sections.label: Exposure before index case detection
sections.summary: Much of the exposure and risk happens before the COVID-19 index case is detected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In truth, much of the exposure and the risk will happen before the COVID-19 index case is detected.

sections.label: COVID-19 risk context for public
sections.summary: Risks of COVID-19 infection, complications and severe disease should be put in context relative to other diseases like influenza and dengue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The relative risks of COVID-19 infection and getting the infection and then perhaps risks of complications and severe disease and put these in context relative to other common diseases, such as influenza, or even not so common diseases, such as dengue, for the public to understand how they should go about their business when we reach some sort of equilibrium.

sections.label: Minister Ong on projected daily cases
sections.summary: Minister Ong Ye Kung said on 21 September that during the preparatory period, MOH projected handling 100 to 200 cases a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Ong Ye Kung said on 21 September that during the preparatory period, MOH projected handling 100 to 200 cases a day.

sections.label: Daily case number projections
sections.summary: In late August, a possible daily number of 3,200 was mentioned if the doubling cycle goes on five times, and the source of the 100 and 200 number is unclear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for the numbers, if I remember correctly, in late August, when we started seeing a wave, I mentioned 3,200 as a possible daily number, if the doubling cycle goes on five times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The "100 and 200" number, I am not sure where it comes from.

sections.label: Home recovery for children under 12
sections.summary: Children under 12 can serve home recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for children under 12, actually, they can serve home recovery.

sections.label: Availability of manpower and resources
sections.summary: The answer is yes because manpower, beds and resources are available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The answer is yes, because manpower, beds and resources are available.

sections.label: Screening and test centres
sections.summary: There are 22 Regional Screening Centres, 20 Quick Test Centres and five private Quick Test Centres, with work to open them to other users and employers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: He has identified the direction in which we are moving with these strategies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have 22 Regional Screening Centres, 20 Quick Test Centres and five private Quick Test Centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are already working on opening up these areas to other users and working with the employers as well, just to make sure these resources are made available to as wide a base as possible, to speed up the processes that he talks about.

sections.label: Hawker centre testing centres
sections.summary: Existing hawker centre centres are prioritised for the employees they were set up to serve, while the Government works to incentivise private vendors to set up more convenient centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And the ones, particularly in the hawker centres, that the Member talked about, are available, but they are prioritised on the basis of how they were set up for the employees that they are meant to serve.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But in the medium term, we are working with other parts of the Government to incentivise private vendors; perhaps, through a grant scheme, and our intent is to then set up more centres which can be more convenient in other locations for the community and larger groups of workers.

sections.label: Previous planning parameters questioned
sections.summary: The Member asks about previous planning parameters when the endemic phase was announced, to know whether resources are adequate and avoid long waits for responses.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But my question relates to what were the previous planning parameters when we first announced that we are moving into the endemic phase.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is very key because we need to know that we are properly resourced; that we do not have a situation like what we saw in the last couple of weeks where people were waiting for days, or up to a week, before they were actually responded to.

sections.label: Reviewing COVID-19 protocols
sections.summary: In the phase of living with COVID-19, protocols were announced last weekend to be holistically reviewed with a view to streamline them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But, now, we are in a phase of trying to live with COVID-19 and there are protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we announced last weekend that we are in the process of holistically reviewing all the protocols with a view to streamline them.

sections.label: Case handling capacity
sections.summary: Capacity now handles 3,000 cases and is ramping up in one to two weeks to handle 5,000 cases, though it is unknown whether that will be reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: By now, we have capacity to handle 3,000 cases and ramping up in one to two weeks to handle 5,000 cases – but we do not know whether we will reach there.

sections.label: HRP acknowledged as not going well
sections.summary: The speaker fully acknowledges that what did not go well was the HRP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What I think did not go well, and I fully acknowledge that, was the HRP.

sections.label: HRP improvements and home recovery
sections.summary: Improvements are seen day by day, and HRP must work so that well patients with no or mild symptoms can recover at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, day by day, we are seeing improvements and we will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have to make HRP work, then the great majority of patients who are well, no symptoms, mild symptoms can recover at home.

sections.label: COVID-19 beds set aside
sections.summary: COVID-19 beds are set aside to isolate patients, but under endemic COVID-19 the disease will be treated like any other infectious disease.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the first part, we set aside COVID-19 beds currently because our approach is to isolate them and separate them from the rest of the patients in the healthcare facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But as you go towards endemic COVID-19, COVID-19 will have to be treated like any other infectious disease.

sections.label: Ramping up capacity during surge
sections.summary: During the surge, capacity is ramped up and resources mobilised, and patient flow improved, though COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 beds cannot be delineated in the steady state.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: They will have kidney problems, heart problems and neurological problems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, it is a bit hard to then delineate, in the steady state, once we are done with the surge, once we are done with this current strategy, as we move towards endemic COVID-19, I do not think we will be in a position to then say, these are the COVID-19 beds and these are the non-COVID-19 beds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Nevertheless, in the middle of the surge now, we are ramping up our capacity, mobilising resources, as we have described in our answers to Parliamentary Questions and supplementary questions, but also trying to improve the flow of patients through our system, so that these resources are made available.
